description: Black-and-white line drawing of one cell in mitosis. The cell is a bold oval outline. At the top pole and again at the bottom pole sits a pair of small solid black dots (a centriole pair) with short radiating aster lines fanning out around it. Fine spindle fibres arc from the top pole to the bottom pole through the interior. Eight short, thick, solid-black chromatids — drawn as V-shapes and hooks — are spread through the cell, four in the upper half and four in the lower half, oriented as though being drawn apart toward opposite poles. A leader line entering from the left carries the printed words 'Chromosome (sister chromatid)' and terminates on the leftmost upper chromatid. A separate leader arrow from the upper right carries a bold 'X' and its arrowhead lands on one of the spindle fibres running down from the top pole.
notes: LIVE — and fit to be on a card. Q3 (Section A); the diagram serves parts (a)–(g), with (c) 'Identify the part labelled X' and (e) 'What is the diploid number of this cell?' (eight chromatids are drawn, four per pole). The whole cell, both poles, all eight chromatids and the X leader sit inside the crop with clear white margin on every side; no ink touches any edge. One line of question prose ('following in relation to mitosis.') sits above the figure and a clipped '(a) Name the stage of mitosis shown in the diagram' below — prose only, the picture itself is untouched. Note for the card author: the only worded label on the figure is 'Chromosome (sister chromatid)', which is NOT attached to a letter, so it is not recorded in labelMeanings; X is printed bare and must be decoded from the marking scheme.

description: A three-panel sequence illustrating enzyme action, with a bold black arrow between panel 1 and panel 2 and another between panel 2 and panel 3. Panel 1: a large pale-grey blob with a jagged notch cut into its right side (a C-shape); the word 'Enzyme' with a vertical arrow points down into the body of this blob, and a bold 'A' with a diagonal arrow points to a small mid-grey shape sitting just outside the notch whose profile matches the notch. Panel 2: the same pale-grey blob with the small mid-grey shape now seated inside the notch; a bold 'B' sits above the panel on a square bracket that spans the whole combined structure. Panel 3: the pale-grey blob again with its notch empty, and to its right two separate darker-grey fragments; a bold 'C' at the top right has two arrows, one to each fragment.
notes: LIVE — and fit to be on a card. Q4 (Section A): (a) identify A and B, (b) which theory of enzyme action, (c) what type of metabolic reaction (one substrate becomes two products, so the sequence is a breakdown). No ink touches any edge — verified pixel-wise. This file was re-cropped on 4 Aug (mtime later than every other file in the batch) and the earlier, defective extraction of the same figure survives as biology-2021-HL-paper1-p06-i1.png; use THIS one, not i1. The word 'Enzyme' is a leader label not tied to any letter, so it is not in labelMeanings; A, B and C are printed bare.

description: Left two-thirds: the printed stem and parts (i)–(vii) of question 14(b). Right third: a greyscale shaded drawing of a three-dimensional block of intestinal lining, cut open at the front to show a longitudinal section through a villus. Four finger-like villi rise from the block; the front one is sectioned so its interior is exposed. Inside that villus a dense meshwork of fine looping vessels runs the full height, wrapped around a single straight vessel that runs up the centre. The outer surface of the villus is drawn as a beaded, brush-like layer of cells. Below the villi the block shows a thin banded layer, then a basal strip containing a cross-sectioned circular vessel (drawn with a ring of dark dots), a second smaller circular vessel, and wavy fibre bundles. Three leader labels come in from the left: the word 'Epithelium' on a short diagonal arrow to the beaded outer surface near the villus tip; a bold 'X' on a horizontal arrow to the single straight central vessel; and the words 'Blood capillary' on a horizontal arrow to one strand of the surrounding looping vessel network.
notes: LIVE — and fit to be on a card. Verified against a full render of paper 2 page 5: the entire villus block, all four villi, both worded leaders and the X leader are present, with white margin at top, left and right. The only edge contact is 51 dark pixels on the bottom row, which is the clipped start of part (c) prose ('The transpiration stream has an important role...') — question prose, not the picture, so not counted as truncation. 'Epithelium' and 'Blood capillary' are worded leaders not attached to letters, so they are not in labelMeanings; X is printed bare and Q14(b)(iii) asks the student to name it. One gap for a later wave: the Q14(c) 'Plant / Stomatal density' table (A 43, B 28, C 68) further down page 5 is vector text in the PDF and was NOT extracted as an image, so no crop exists for 14(c).

description: A clean black-line drawing of a flower cut in longitudinal section, with the stem end at the lower right. Two large pointed petals dominate — one sweeping up and to the left, one pointing left and slightly down. Three stamens are drawn as long slender filaments each tipped with an elongated, capsule-shaped anther: one arching over the top right, one projecting to the upper left, one hanging to the lower left. At the centre of the flower sits a rough, jagged-edged mass. Below and behind it, fine hair-like filaments hang down in a dense tuft, and a smooth swollen chamber with a curved lip runs off to the right. Four horizontal leader arrows come in from the right, stacked top to bottom: 'A' to the anther arching over the top right; 'B' to the upper surface of the large upper petal; 'C' to the jagged central mass; 'D' to the tuft of fine hair-like filaments below the centre.
notes: LIVE — and fit to be on a card. Verified against a full render of paper 2 page 6: the whole flower, all three stamens, the ovary chamber and all four leader arrows are inside the crop. The 6 dark pixels on the bottom row are descenders from the clipped question line '(i) Name the structures labelled A, B and C.' — prose, so not counted. All four letters are printed BARE: the figure names nothing in words, so labelMeanings is deliberately empty. Do not let a card infer A/B/C/D from the question stem — Q15(b)(i) only asks for A, B and C, while (iv) asks the role of A and D and (vi)(1) asks which labelled part becomes the fruit, so the scheme must supply all four.

description: A greyscale shaded drawing of a three-dimensional block of human skin, cut open at the front to show a section from the surface down. Five hairs project up and to the left from the top surface. Just under the surface is a thin banded layer; below it a pale bulk fills most of the block, and along the bottom sits a thick grey layer of rounded globules. Running down the left of the section is a long dark tapering shaft holding the root of one hair, with a pale multi-lobed gland pressed against its upper right side and a pale band running diagonally down from it. In the middle of the block an inverted-U loop of tube, cross-hatched along its crown, sits high in the section at the top of a long dark tube that descends to the base, with fine branching vessels spreading off it. At the lower right a tight round ball of coiled tubing is connected by a wavy dark duct that climbs to a pore at the surface. A branching, tree-like vessel network spreads through the right of the block and a horizontal vessel network runs along the base. Three arrows: 'A' on a horizontal arrow from the left, its head landing where the dark hair shaft meets the pale lobed gland; 'B' on a horizontal arrow from the right to the cross-hatched inverted-U loop; 'C' on a horizontal arrow from the right, lower down, to the tight ball of coiled tubing.
notes: LIVE — and fit to be on a card. Verified against a full render of paper 2 page 7: the complete skin block, all five hairs, the basal layer and all three arrows are inside the crop with white margin left and right. The 211 dark pixels on the bottom row are the clipped question line '(i) Which labelled structure is involved in vasoconstriction?' — question prose, not the picture, so not counted as truncation. All three letters are printed bare; the figure names nothing in words, hence labelMeanings is empty. One caution worth passing on: A's arrowhead lands almost exactly on the boundary between the dark hair shaft and the pale lobed gland beside it, so a card writing its own gloss for A should follow the marking scheme rather than the pixel.

description: A line graph with no numeric scale or tick marks on either axis. The vertical axis is labelled, in three stacked lines to its left, 'Relative antibody concentration'; the horizontal axis is labelled 'Time (days)' beneath its centre. A single continuous curve runs left to right along the baseline: it stays flat, then rises into a low, narrow, rounded bump, falls back to a slightly raised plateau, then climbs steeply into a second peak that is far taller and much broader than the first, holds briefly at its summit, falls away steeply, and levels off into a plateau roughly a third of the peak height that continues to the right end of the curve. Two bold labels with diagonal arrows mark points on the baseline: 'A' points down to the baseline at the far left, before the small bump; 'B' points down to the baseline at the foot of the steep second climb.
notes: LIVE — and fit to be on a card. No ink touches any edge, verified pixel-wise; both axis titles, both arrows and the whole curve are inside the frame with generous white margin. Note for a card author: the axes carry NO units or numbers — the y-axis is 'Relative antibody concentration' and the x-axis is 'Time (days)' with no scale — so any question asking a student to read a value off this graph would be unanswerable. Q16(c)(v) correctly asks only for a comparison of the response at A (after vaccination) with the response at B (after infection) and a reason. A and B are printed bare.

description: A pen-and-ink drawing of a single large amoeboid cell: an irregular blob with several blunt, lobed pseudopodia, its outline drawn as one continuous line and its cytoplasm filled with fine stippled dots. Inside it, left of centre, is a large oval body packed with much denser stippling. Upper-middle sits a clear, unstippled circle. Scattered through the cytoplasm are four or five small oval bodies each containing a dark granular inclusion. On the right side the outline is drawn into a deep notch, and a small oval organism with a dark granular interior lies in that notch, partly cupped by the cell's cytoplasm. Labels: a bold 'B' at the upper left on a long arrow to the clear unstippled circle; the word 'Nucleus' at the lower left on an arrow to the large densely stippled oval; a bold 'A' at the upper right sitting on a square bracket that spans the finger-like pseudopodium immediately above the notch; the italic word 'Euglena' at the right on a leader to the small oval organism in the notch; a bold 'C' at the lower right on an arrow to one of the small oval bodies with a dark inclusion in the lower-middle of the cytoplasm.
notes: LIVE — and fit to be on a card. Verified against a full render of paper 2 page 9: the whole cell, every pseudopodium, all three letters and both worded leaders are inside the crop. Row 0 carries 244 dark pixels, but that is the question line '(b) The diagram below shows a unicellular organism.' sliced through mid-letter at the top boundary — question prose, so NOT counted as truncation; the drawing itself begins well below it and is whole. One cosmetic improvement a later wave could make: recrop 8–10px lower to drop that half-cut prose line, since the card prints its own stem and the sliced text looks like damage. 'Nucleus' and 'Euglena' are worded leaders not attached to letters, so they stay out of labelMeanings; A, B and C are printed bare. Beware the index order on this page — the figure numbered i0 is question 17(b), while 17(a) is the file numbered i1, the reverse of reading order down the page.

description: A pen-and-ink drawing of a filamentous mould. Four upright stalks rise from two clusters on a horizontal surface; each stalk swells at its tip into a round head speckled with dots, three of them intact at the top right and one at the left drawn as an open, emptying head. From that open head a loose cloud of small circles drifts up and to the left. The stalks meet the surface at two junction points, and from each junction fine strands run away horizontally, left and right, linking the clusters. Below each junction a spreading tuft of thin, repeatedly branching root-like filaments descends. Labels: the word 'Spores' at the upper left with two arrows pointing into the cloud of small circles; a bold 'A' at the top with a diagonal arrow whose head lands on the upright stalk just below the tallest round head; a bold 'B' at the right with two arrows, one to the horizontal strand running left from the right-hand junction and one to the horizontal strand running right from it; the word 'Rhizoid' at the lower left on an arrow to one of the branching root-like filaments.
notes: LIVE — and fit to be on a card. Verified against a full render of paper 2 page 9: every stalk and head, the spore cloud, both horizontal strands and both rhizoid tufts are inside the crop, with white margin at top, left and right. The 136 dark pixels on the bottom row are the clipped question lines '(i) Name the organism shown in the diagram and the kingdom to which it belongs.' / '(ii) Name the part labelled A' — question prose, not counted. 'Spores' and 'Rhizoid' are worded leaders not tied to a letter, so labelMeanings stays empty; A and B are printed bare. Caution for the card author: A's arrowhead lands on the STALK just below the round head, not on the head itself, so the gloss for A must come from the marking scheme, not from the picture. Index-order warning as above — this is 17(a) despite being the i1 file.

description: Two side-by-side rectangular greyscale micrograph-style panels of plant epidermal cells, each with a bold letter above it and a caption below. Left panel, headed 'A' and captioned 'Epidermal cells in solution A': roughly a dozen elongated brick-shaped cells packed edge to edge in a tile pattern, each cell filled edge to edge with uniform mid-grey shading, the cell boundaries showing as thin bright white lines, and each cell containing one small dark round dot. Right panel, headed 'B' and captioned 'Epidermal cells in solution B': the same tiled arrangement of cells, but in every cell the mid-grey shaded region has shrunk into a rounded, irregular mass pulled inward and away from the cell boundary, leaving a broad pale gap between the shaded mass and the outer wall; the small dark round dot sits within each shrunken mass and the wall outlines remain in their original positions.

description: A black-line drawing of a spinal cord in cross section with a reflex pathway attached. On the right, the cord is drawn as a broad outline enclosing a butterfly-shaped inner region with a small open circle at its centre; a deep V-shaped fissure notches the top of the outline and a shallower notch the bottom. From the left of the cord two roots emerge. The upper root carries a nerve fibre that runs left, passing through a small circle-with-a-dot swelling on its way, and curves down to the left. The lower root carries a second fibre that runs left and curves down. Inside the butterfly-shaped region are two further circle-with-a-dot markings joined by a short fibre with small forked terminals drawn at each end. Labels: a bold 'X' at the top on a vertical arrow pointing down to the outer boundary line of the cord beside the top fissure; 'Neuron B' on an arrow to the upper root fibre where it enters the cord; 'Neuron A' on an arrow to the lower root fibre where it enters the cord; 'Neuron C' on an arrow to the short fibre linking the two markings inside the butterfly region. At the left, two rectangular boxes containing the words 'Receptor' and 'Effector' sit at the ends of the two fibres, the Receptor box slightly higher and further left than the Effector box.

description: A sectioned front view of the human heart on the right two-thirds of the crop, drawn cut open with its two halves in different tones: the half on the viewer's left is light grey, the half on the viewer's right is dark grey, separated by a vertical dividing wall. White block arrows inside the chambers and vessels trace the direction of blood flow. Four large vessels leave the top of the heart — one sloping down to the upper left, two rising side by side at the centre, and one sloping down to the upper right. A valve is drawn where each upper chamber meets the lower chamber beneath it, and the muscular wall closes to a rounded apex at the bottom. Labels: A, a vertical arrow pointing down onto the vessel entering at the upper left; B, an arrow pointing left onto the top of the left-hand of the two central rising vessels (light grey); C, an arrow pointing left onto the top of the right-hand central rising vessel (dark grey); D, a long arrow pointing left onto the valve inside the dark-grey half between its upper and lower chambers; E, a long arrow pointing right onto the vertical wall dividing the two lower chambers. Two further parts are named in words, not letters: 'Right atrium' with an arrow into the light-grey upper chamber, and 'Left ventricle' with an arrow into the dark-grey lower chamber. The left third of the crop carries the printed Q13(b)(i)-(v) prose.
notes: LIVE and fit to be on a card. Verified at zoom that all four great vessels, both word labels, all five letters and the apex sit inside the frame with white margin. labelMeanings is empty by design: the figure names two parts in words ('Right atrium', 'Left ventricle') but neither is tied to a letter, so A-E are bare letters and must be decoded from the marking scheme. Q13(b)(i) asks which letter is the septum, vena cava, aorta and bicuspid valve, and (b)(iii) and (b)(iv) refer back to B and D, so every letter has to render legibly — they all do.

description: A black-line drawing of the human digestive system, centred. From the top a narrow tube descends and curves right into a large sac-like organ on the upper right. A short looping tube runs down from between them and joins a long, frilly-edged, elongated organ that runs away to the right. Below, a wide roughly rectangular loop of gut encircles a mass of tightly coiled narrow intestine, with a short blind projection at the lower left and a terminal tube descending at the bottom centre. Labels: B, arrow pointing right into the large upper-left organ; 'Gall bladder', arrow pointing right onto the small pear-shaped sac; A, arrow pointing right onto the looping tube just below the gall bladder; C, arrow pointing left into the large upper-right sac; D, arrow pointing left onto the frilly elongated organ; E, arrow pointing left onto the outer wide loop of gut. The stem '(b) The diagram shows the human digestive system.' is printed above and '(i) Name the parts labelled A, B, C, D, E.' below.
notes: LIVE and fit to be on a card. Compared side by side against a render of PDF page 5 — the crop reproduces the whole artwork with margin on all sides, including the top of the oesophagus tube and the terminal tube at the bottom. labelMeanings is empty because 'Gall bladder' is a given word label not tied to any letter; A-E are bare and come from the marking scheme. Keep the 'Gall bladder' label visible: Q14(b)(iii) ('What liquid is stored in the gall bladder?') leans on it.

description: A wide horizontal, micrograph-style drawing of the path water takes from the soil into a root, in longitudinal section. On the left are four dark, heavily stippled irregular lumps (soil particles) with a long, very narrow, thin-walled tube running out between them to the left. To their right stand several columns of large, pale, thick-walled root cells drawn with double cell walls and small dark nuclei. Further right is a narrow column of much smaller, elongated cells, and at the far right two tall vertical vessels whose walls are drawn as continuous cross-hatched spiral or ring-like thickenings. Solid grey block arrows trace the route: in along the narrow tube, then stepwise from cell to cell across the columns of large cells, then into the two right-hand vessels, where two further grey arrows point straight upwards. Labels: 'Soil particles' at the top left with two arrows to two of the dark lumps; A at the lower left with an arrow up and right onto the long narrow tube; and beneath the drawing two square brackets with stems — C under the narrow column of small cells and B under the two cross-hatched vessels.
notes: LIVE and fit to be on a card. Verified against a render of PDF page 6 (image bbox 142-497 x 116-261 pt): the crop contains the entire artwork with margin, and the right-hand vessels end cleanly inside the frame. Note the artwork's OWN rectangular boundary slices the topmost and bottom-most row of cells — that is how it is printed in the paper, not an extraction cut, so truncated is correctly false. Important for card layout: B and C are bracket labels UNDER the figure, not arrow labels, so a card must render the bottom strip or both letters lose their referents. Q15(b) parts (ii)-(viii) refer to A, B and C throughout.

description: A surface (plan) view of the under surface of a leaf on the right of the crop, drawn as a patch of grey, brick-like, irregular interlocking cells with faint texture lines. Scattered across the patch are five stomata, each drawn as a darker grey oval pair of cells enclosing a white, lens-shaped slit. Labels: X, a long arrow pointing left onto the white slit of the top-left stoma; Y, a long arrow pointing left onto the darker oval cell surrounding the slit of the second stoma at the upper right; and 'Dermal cells' at the bottom right with a leader line running up and left to a plain grey cell in the lower right of the patch. The left half of the crop carries the heading 'The diagram below shows the under surface of a leaf.' and the printed Q15(c)(iii)-(vii) prose.
notes: LIVE and fit to be on a card. Both letters, both arrows, the whole cell patch and the 'Dermal cells' annotation are inside the frame with margin. One caution for card rendering: X marks the pore and Y marks the cell around a pore, and their arrowheads are only about 40 px apart at native size — show this crop at full width or students cannot tell the two apart. labelMeanings is empty because 'Dermal cells' is not tied to a letter; X and Y are bare and come from the marking scheme.

description: A bold black-line sectioned diagram of the human ear, facing left. On the left is the outer ear (pinna) with its folds, rim and lobe; from it a wide canal runs right and slightly downwards to an oval membrane closing its inner end. Beyond the membrane is an air-filled cavity containing a chain of three small, irregularly shaped bones. To the right of that cavity, three interlocking loops rise at the top and a flat spiral shell sits below them; a tapering nerve runs off to the right from the spiral, and a narrow double-walled tube runs down and to the right from the cavity. Labels: A, arrow pointing left onto the three loops at the top; B, arrow pointing left onto the spiral; C, arrow pointing up and right onto the oval membrane at the inner end of the canal; 'Auditory nerve', arrow pointing left onto the tapering nerve at the right; 'Middle ear', a vertical line with an arrow pointing up into the bone-containing cavity; 'Eustachian tube', arrow pointing left onto the narrow descending tube. The stem '(a) The diagram shows the human ear.' is printed above and '(i) Name the part labelled A and give its function.' below.
notes: LIVE and fit to be on a card. All three letters and all three word labels are inside the frame with white margin. description: A simple black-line drawing of the human urinary system, front view. Two bean-shaped organs sit one either side, each with an indented inner margin. From each of those inner margins a long narrow tube descends and curves inwards to meet a rounded sac at the bottom centre, and a single short tube leaves the bottom of that sac. description: A black-line sectioned diagram of a foetus in the womb before birth, front view. The womb is a pear-shaped chamber with a thick double-lined wall; inside it a foetus lies curled head-down, knees drawn up, one arm folded across the chest, head at the bottom. Attached to the inner wall on the upper left is a stippled, frilly-edged mass whose finger-like projections grip the wall, and a thick banded cord runs from that mass across to the foetus's abdomen. From the top corners of the womb two narrow tubes run up and outwards, each ending in a small circle. At the base the womb wall narrows to a short neck, below which a further passage opens out. Labels: A, a vertical arrow pointing up onto the tube on the upper left; B, a vertical arrow pointing up onto the circle at the end of the tube on the upper right; C, an arrow pointing left onto the narrow neck at the base of the womb. Three further parts are named in words: 'Placenta' with an arrow to the stippled frilly mass, 'Umbilical cord' with an arrow to the banded cord, and 'Womb wall' with an arrow to the thick wall on the right. The Q17(a) stem is above and '(i) Identify the structures labelled A, B, C on the diagram.' below.

Watch A against B — A's arrowhead lands part-way ALONG the left tube while B's lands on the CIRCLE at the end of the right tube, so they are not symmetrical and must not be assumed to mark the same structure. labelMeanings is empty because none of the three word labels is tied to a letter. description: A grey diagram of a single neuron drawn side-on, running left to right. On the left is a star-shaped cell body with roughly eight tapering, branching processes radiating from it and one small dark circular body inside it. From the right of the cell body a long process runs horizontally away; along it sit four separate pale, lumpy, sausage-shaped sheath segments, each separated from the next by a short bare constriction of the process. At the far right the process divides into several fine branches, each ending in a small rounded knob. Labels: A, a long horizontal arrow pointing right onto the small dark circular body inside the cell body; B, a single letter with TWO arrows fanning out to two different branching processes at the upper left; C, a vertical arrow pointing down onto one of the pale sheath segments; D, a vertical arrow pointing up onto the bare constriction between two sheath segments. The stem '(d) The diagram shows a neuron.' is sliced horizontally through the middle by the top edge, and '(i) Name the parts A, B, C, D.' is printed below.
notes: LIVE and fit to be on a card. The whole neuron from dendrite tips to terminal knobs, and all four letters, are inside the frame with margin. Two things a card must get right: B carries TWO arrowheads to two different processes (it labels a class of structure, not one point), and C and D are only a few millimetres apart on the same process — C on a sheath segment, D on the gap between segments — so the crop must be shown large enough to distinguish them. description: A diagram of a rod-shaped (capsule-shaped) bacterial cell in section, drawn wide and horizontal with rounded ends. description: A stylised cut-away diagram of a spherical coronavirus particle. A grey circular envelope is studded all round its rim with club- or mushroom-headed spike projections on short stalks, with short bars embedded in the envelope wall between them. A leader line runs from a bold letter 'A' at the left to the short squiggle. Separate from the particle, to its right, sits a small square outlined box containing a bold 'X'.
notes: LIVE — fit to be on a card, with one caveat a card author must handle. description: A simple black-outline side-view diagram of the human male reproductive system. description: A line diagram of a section through the spinal cord with attached nerves. The bold letter B in the middle has a horizontal arrow pointing left into a short fibre lying inside the grey matter between the upper and lower cells. The bold letter C at the bottom has an arrow running up-right to a second ring-and-dot cell body in the lower lobe of the grey matter, whose fibre runs out to the right to a boxed word label reading 'Effector'. A clipped fragment of the line '(a) The diagram shows a section through the spinal cord with attached nerves.' sits at the top edge.
notes: LIVE — and fit to be on a card. description: Greyscale transmission electron micrograph of rod-shaped (bacillus) bacteria. Two further partial cells sit at the top-left and bottom-right corners. A boxed capital X is printed on the pale background at the top of the picture, just left of centre. description: Absorption spectrum of the two chlorophylls. Y-axis: a plain arrow labelled "Absorption of light" (rotated, bold, no numeric scale or units). X-axis: labelled "Colour of light" (bold) beneath a grey banded strip whose six segments are named in italics left to right — Violet, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red. A legend inside the plot reads "Chlorophyll a" against a dotted line sample and "Chlorophyll b" against a solid line sample. The dotted (chlorophyll a) trace has a moderate peak over Violet, sinks to near-zero across Green/Yellow/Orange, and rises to its tallest peak over Red. The solid (chlorophyll b) trace rises from Violet to a tall narrow peak over Blue, runs low across the middle with a slight bump under Yellow, and has a second peak at the Orange/Red boundary that is slightly shorter than the dotted red peak. One line of question prose ("Answer the following questions based on the graph and the process of photosynthesis.") sits above the graph.
notes: LIVE — fit to be on a card. Whole graph present: both axes, the y-axis title, the full colour band, the legend and both complete traces; the bold "Colour of light" title clears the bottom edge by 3 px. lettersVisible is deliberately empty: the only letters on the figure are the italic a and b inside the printed words "Chlorophyll a" and "Chlorophyll b" in the legend, which are species names the figure spells out itself, not bare part-identifiers needing a decode. Which trace is which matters for 7(a)(i)/(ii) — the legend, not the crop's filename, is the authority: dotted = chlorophyll a, solid = chlorophyll b.
